q: A contract signed by a 16-year-old to buy a car is generally:
e: Minors usually lack full contractual capacity, so most contracts they sign are voidable — the minor may choose to cancel.

q: Which element is NOT required to form a valid contract?
e: Many contracts are valid orally. The required elements are agreement, consideration, capacity and legality; only some contracts must be written.

q: A company registers its logo so competitors cannot use it. The logo is protected by a:
e: Trademarks protect words, names, symbols or logos that identify the source of goods or services.

q: In a general partnership, each partner's liability for business debts is:
e: General partners have unlimited personal liability, unlike shareholders or LLC members.

q: An employer refuses to promote an employee because of her religion. Which law is most directly violated?
c: Title VII of the Civil Rights Act
e: Title VII prohibits employment discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex and national origin.

q: Two competing gas stations secretly agree to charge the same high price. This is:
e: Agreements between competitors to set prices are price fixing, illegal under antitrust law.

q: Failing to perform the duties stated in a contract is called:
e: Breach of contract occurs when a party fails to fulfill its contractual obligations without a legal excuse.

q: Which business ownership form protects owners from personal liability while allowing profits to pass through to their personal tax returns?
e: An LLC offers limited liability plus pass-through taxation by default.

q: Restating what a speaker said in your own words to confirm understanding is called:
e: Paraphrasing is an active listening technique that confirms meaning.

q: Which is the best way to begin a persuasive business presentation?
c: Open with an attention-getter tied to the audience's need
e: A strong opener captures attention and connects to what the audience cares about.

q: Crossed arms, little eye contact and leaning away are examples of:
e: Body language is nonverbal communication and often signals defensiveness or disinterest.

q: When writing a business email to a client, you should:
c: Put the main point or request near the beginning
Write in all capital letters for emphasis
e: Effective business writing is direct; readers should see the purpose quickly.

q: Information that flows from a manager down to employees is called:
e: Downward communication moves from higher to lower levels of the organization.

q: A staff meeting is most effective when the leader:
e: An agenda sets purpose, keeps the meeting on track and lets attendees prepare.

q: The 'noise' in the communication process refers to:
c: Anything that interferes with the message
e: Noise is any barrier — physical, psychological or semantic — that distorts the message.

q: Which is an example of a closed-ended question?
c: What did you like about the service?
Did you receive your order on time?
e: Closed-ended questions can be answered with yes/no or a short fact.

q: When giving directions to a new employee, it is best to:
c: Give all steps at once quickly
Explain steps in logical order and check for understanding
Assume they will ask if confused
e: Sequential steps plus a comprehension check reduce errors.

q: A customer is angry about a late delivery. The FIRST thing an employee should do is:
c: Listen without interrupting and acknowledge the frustration
e: Listening and empathizing calms the customer before problem-solving.

q: Customer relationship management (CRM) primarily aims to:
e: CRM uses customer data and interactions to strengthen long-term relationships.

q: A hotel remembers a returning guest's preferred room type. This demonstrates:
e: Using customer history to tailor service is personalization, which builds loyalty.

q: It is generally true that acquiring a new customer costs ____ retaining an existing one.
e: Acquisition typically costs several times more than retention, which is why loyalty matters.

q: A company's brand promise is best reinforced when:
c: Advertising differs from the actual experience
Every employee interaction delivers what was promised
e: Consistency between promise and experience builds trust in the brand.

q: Which is an example of a customer-service policy that builds goodwill?
e: Generous, clear policies reduce risk for customers and build goodwill.

q: When the price of a good rises and quantity demanded falls, this illustrates:
e: The law of demand: price and quantity demanded move in opposite directions.

q: The value of the next-best alternative given up when making a choice is:
e: Opportunity cost is what you sacrifice by choosing one option over another.

q: Gross domestic product (GDP) measures:
c: The market value of all final goods and services produced in a country in a period
e: GDP is the total value of final goods and services produced within a country.

q: A market with one seller and no close substitutes is a:
e: A monopoly has a single seller controlling supply.

q: If demand for a product is elastic, raising its price will most likely:
e: With elastic demand, quantity falls proportionally more than price rises, so revenue drops.

q: A general, sustained increase in prices across the economy is:
e: Inflation reduces the purchasing power of money.

q: The Federal Reserve raising interest rates is typically intended to:
c: Lower the value of the dollar
e: Higher rates make borrowing costlier, cooling spending and inflation.

q: A tax placed on imported goods is called a:
e: A tariff is a tax on imports; a quota limits quantity; an embargo bans trade.

q: The basic economic problem that all societies face is:
e: Unlimited wants and limited resources create scarcity, forcing choices.

q: Recognizing your own emotions and how they affect your behavior is called:
e: Self-awareness is the foundation of emotional intelligence.

q: A coworker receives criticism and responds calmly, asking how to improve. This shows:
e: Self-regulation is managing emotional reactions constructively.

q: Understanding a teammate's feelings from their point of view is:
e: Empathy is understanding and sharing another person's perspective.

q: Which statement is the most assertive (not aggressive or passive)?
c: 'I'd like to finish my point, then I'll hear yours.'
e: Assertive communication states needs clearly and respectfully.

q: Two team members disagree on a plan. The best first step to resolve the conflict is to:
c: Have the manager pick a winner
e: Understanding interests behind positions opens up solutions both can accept.

q: Ethical behavior in the workplace is best described as:
c: Acting according to moral principles even when not required
e: Ethics goes beyond legality to doing what is right.

q: A leader who adapts style to the team's experience and the situation is using:
e: Situational leaders adjust direction and support to followers' readiness.

q: Which behavior best demonstrates trustworthiness at work?
e: Reliability and honesty build trust.

q: Showing initiative on the job means:
c: Doing tasks that need to be done without being told
e: Initiative is acting proactively on what needs to be done.

q: When giving constructive feedback, you should focus on:
e: Behavior-focused, specific feedback is actionable and less threatening.

q: Adjusting quickly when a project's priorities suddenly change demonstrates:
e: Adaptability is adjusting effectively to change.

q: An entrepreneur's main reason for writing a business plan is to:
c: Guide the business and attract financing
e: A business plan maps strategy and shows investors/lenders the opportunity.

q: Buying the right to operate a business using an established brand and system is a:
e: Franchisees pay for the brand and operating system of a franchisor.

q: Money invested in a startup in exchange for ownership is:
e: Equity financing trades ownership for capital; no repayment required.

q: A minimum viable product (MVP) is used to:
c: Launch a finished product at full scale
Test the core idea with real customers at low cost
e: An MVP validates demand quickly before heavy investment.

q: Which personal trait is most associated with successful entrepreneurs?
e: Entrepreneurs take calculated, not reckless, risks.

q: Identifying an unmet customer need that a business can profitably fill is recognizing a(n):
e: Opportunity recognition is the starting point of venture creation.

q: An angel investor is typically:
c: A wealthy individual who funds early-stage startups
e: Angels invest personal funds in early ventures, often for equity.

q: Assets = Liabilities + ______
e: The accounting equation: Assets = Liabilities + Owner's Equity.

q: Which financial statement shows revenues and expenses over a period?
e: The income statement reports profit or loss over a period.

q: A business has current assets of $60,000 and current liabilities of $30,000. Its current ratio is:
e: Current ratio = current assets ÷ current liabilities = 60,000 ÷ 30,000 = 2.0.

q: Fixed costs are $10,000, price is $25 and variable cost is $15 per unit. The break-even point is:
e: Break-even = fixed costs ÷ (price − variable cost) = 10,000 ÷ 10 = 1,000 units.

q: A budget is primarily used to:
c: Plan and control future income and spending
e: Budgets are forward-looking financial plans used for control.

q: Revenue of $200,000 and cost of goods sold of $120,000 gives a gross profit margin of:
Which is a current liability?
e: Current liabilities are due within one year, like accounts payable.

q: Spreading the cost of equipment over its useful life is called:
e: Depreciation allocates the cost of tangible assets over time.

q: Return on investment (ROI) is calculated as:
e: ROI = net gain divided by the cost of the investment.

q: A company can be profitable but still run out of cash because:
c: Sales on credit and timing of payments differ from when revenue is recorded
e: Cash flow timing (receivables, inventory, payables) can diverge from accrual profit.

q: Money owed TO a business by its customers is recorded as:
e: Accounts receivable is an asset representing customer balances owed.

q: The process of verifying that a company's financial statements are accurate is a(n):
e: Audits examine records to verify accuracy and compliance.

q: Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) exist to:
c: Make financial statements consistent and comparable
e: GAAP standardizes reporting so users can compare companies.

q: Recording revenue when it is earned, not when cash is received, is the:
e: Accrual accounting recognizes revenue when earned and expenses when incurred.

q: A bank reconciliation compares:
c: The company's cash records with the bank statement
e: Reconciliation finds differences like outstanding checks or errors.

q: In double-entry accounting, every transaction affects at least:
e: Each transaction has equal debits and credits in at least two accounts.

q: Separating the duties of recording, approving and handling cash is an example of:
e: Segregation of duties is an internal control that reduces fraud risk.

q: A written description of a job's duties, responsibilities and requirements is a:
e: Job descriptions guide recruiting, training and evaluation.

q: The process of helping new hires adjust to the company is called:
e: Onboarding integrates new employees into culture and role.

q: High employee turnover usually leads to:
e: Replacing employees is costly in recruiting, training and lost productivity.

q: Health insurance, paid time off and retirement plans are examples of:
e: Benefits are non-wage compensation.

q: Asking all candidates the same set of job-related questions is a(n):
e: Structured interviews improve fairness and comparability.

q: An employee is paid a percentage of each sale they make. This is:
e: Commission ties pay directly to sales results.

q: Data that has been organized and interpreted to be useful for decisions is:
e: Information is processed data with meaning and context.

q: Software used to organize data in rows and columns and perform calculations is a:
e: Spreadsheets handle tabular data and formulas.

q: An email that pretends to be from a bank to steal login details is:
e: Phishing tricks users into revealing sensitive information.

q: Regularly copying data to a separate location protects against loss. This is a:
e: Backups allow recovery after failure, theft or ransomware.

q: Using two forms of verification (e.g., password plus a code texted to your phone) is:
e: MFA greatly reduces unauthorized access.

q: A business that collects customer data has an ethical responsibility to:
c: Protect it and use it as disclosed
e: Privacy and data stewardship are legal and ethical obligations.

q: A visual display of key metrics updated in real time is a:
e: Dashboards summarize KPIs for fast decision-making.

q: Storing files on remote servers accessed through the internet is:
e: Cloud computing delivers storage and software over the internet.

q: Know-how that lives in employees' heads and is hard to write down is:
e: Tacit knowledge comes from experience; capturing it is a key KM challenge.

q: A company creates a searchable internal wiki of best practices. Its main goal is to:
e: Knowledge repositories make expertise reusable across the organization.

q: Pairing a new employee with an experienced one to transfer skills is:
e: Mentoring transfers tacit knowledge person-to-person.

q: Reviewing a finished project to document what worked and what didn't is a:
e: Lessons-learned (after-action) reviews turn experience into reusable knowledge.

q: Comparing your processes to the best performers in your industry is:
e: Benchmarking identifies performance gaps and best practices.

q: An organization that continuously improves by learning from experience is a:
e: Learning organizations build systems for continuous knowledge growth.

q: The 4 Ps of the marketing mix are product, price, place and:
e: The marketing mix: product, price, place (distribution) and promotion.

q: The marketing concept states that a business should:
c: Make what it can, then sell it
Satisfy customer needs while making a profit
e: The marketing concept centers the business on customer satisfaction at a profit.

q: Which is an example of the 'place' (distribution) function?
c: Choosing to sell through grocery chains
e: Place covers channels and getting products to customers.

q: Marketing adds value by creating utility. Having a product available when customers want it is:
e: Time utility = available when needed; place = where needed; possession = ability to own.

q: Dividing a market into groups with similar needs is:
e: Segmentation lets firms target groups with tailored mixes.

q: Keeping just enough inventory, arriving right when needed, is called:
e: JIT lowers carrying costs but requires reliable suppliers.

q: Purchasing goods and services needed to run a business is:
e: Procurement (purchasing) sources inputs at the right quality, price and time.

q: A written step-by-step guide for performing a routine task is a:
e: SOPs make work consistent and easier to train.

q: Which is the BEST example of a safety precaution in a retail store?
e: Warning signs prevent slip-and-fall injuries.

q: The flow of goods from raw materials to the final customer is the:
e: Supply chain management coordinates every step to the customer.

q: Reducing energy and packaging waste to lower costs and environmental impact reflects:
e: Sustainable operations save resources and appeal to customers.

q: Taking a physical count of goods on hand is called:
e: Physical inventory counts verify records and reveal shrinkage.

q: Loss of inventory due to theft, damage or errors is called:
e: Shrinkage reduces profit; controls and audits help limit it.

q: Hiring an outside firm to handle a business function like payroll is:
e: Outsourcing lets a firm focus on core activities.

q: Inventory turnover measures:
c: How many times inventory is sold and replaced in a period
e: Higher turnover means goods sell quickly; low turnover can mean overstock.

q: A brief summary of your skills and goals you can deliver in 30 seconds is an:
e: Elevator pitches make memorable first impressions while networking.

q: A SMART goal is specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and:
e: Time-bound goals have a deadline.

q: After a job interview, it is professional to:
c: Send a thank-you note within a day
Post about it on social media
e: A prompt thank-you reinforces interest and professionalism.

q: Building relationships with people who can share career opportunities is:
e: Networking expands access to information and opportunities.

q: Which is the best example of a transferable skill?
e: Transferable skills apply across jobs and industries.

q: Prioritizing tasks by urgency and importance is a technique of:
e: Time management helps focus effort where it matters most.

q: What you post online can affect job opportunities because employers may review your:
e: Your digital footprint is visible to recruiters; manage it professionally.

q: Continuing to learn new skills throughout your career is called:
e: Lifelong learning keeps skills current as industries change.

q: The three classic project constraints are scope, time and:
e: The 'triple constraint': changing one of scope, time or cost affects the others.

q: A bar chart showing tasks against a timeline is a:
e: Gantt charts visualize schedules and task dependencies.

q: Uncontrolled growth in a project's requirements after it starts is:
e: Scope creep strains budgets and schedules; use change control.

q: The longest sequence of dependent tasks that determines the shortest project duration is the:
e: Any delay on the critical path delays the whole project.

q: Breaking a project into smaller, manageable deliverables is a:
e: A WBS decomposes work so it can be assigned and estimated.

q: A significant point or event in a project schedule is a:
e: Milestones mark progress, such as completing a phase.

q: Anyone affected by or who can affect a project is a:
e: Stakeholder analysis guides communication and buy-in.

q: Continuous, incremental improvement involving all employees is known as:
e: Kaizen is the Japanese philosophy of continuous improvement.

q: Plan-Do-Check-Act is a cycle used for:
e: PDCA (Deming cycle) tests and refines improvements.

q: Inspecting products to catch defects before they reach customers is:
e: Quality control detects defects; quality assurance prevents them in the process.

q: A fishbone (cause-and-effect) diagram is used to:
c: Identify root causes of a problem
e: Ishikawa diagrams organize possible causes into categories.

q: ISO 9001 certification indicates a company:
c: Meets an international quality management standard
e: ISO 9001 certifies a documented quality management system.

q: Six Sigma focuses on:
e: Six Sigma uses data to drive defects toward near zero.

q: Buying insurance to cover potential losses is an example of:
e: Insurance transfers the financial impact of risk to an insurer.

q: A risk that offers only a chance of loss or no loss (like fire) is a:
e: Pure risks can only cause loss; speculative risks can cause gain or loss.

q: Installing security cameras to reduce theft is an example of:
e: Controls that lower likelihood or impact reduce risk.

q: A company decides not to launch a product because legal risks are too high. This is:
e: Avoidance eliminates exposure by not doing the activity.

q: A plan for keeping essential operations running during a disaster is a:
e: Continuity plans reduce downtime from disruptions.

q: Setting aside money to pay for small losses yourself is:
e: Retention (self-insurance) is used for predictable or minor losses.

q: In a SWOT analysis, a new competitor entering the market is a:
e: Threats are external factors that could harm the business.

q: A statement describing an organization's purpose and what it does is its:
e: Mission = purpose today; vision = desired future.

q: Key performance indicators (KPIs) are used to:
e: KPIs are metrics tied to strategic objectives.

q: The four functions of management are planning, organizing, leading and:
e: Controlling compares performance to plans and corrects course.

q: Setting long-term goals for the whole organization is done at which planning level?
e: Strategic plans are long-range and set by top management.

q: A company buying one of its suppliers is an example of:
e: Vertical integration expands along the supply chain.

q: A backup plan prepared in case the main plan fails is a:
e: Contingency plans prepare responses to possible disruptions.

q: A channel where the manufacturer sells directly to consumers is a:
e: Direct channels have no intermediaries (e.g., brand website).

q: A business that buys in bulk from producers and sells to retailers is a:
e: Wholesalers break bulk and distribute to retailers.

q: Selling a product in as many outlets as possible is:
e: Intensive distribution suits convenience goods like gum.

q: A luxury watch brand sold in only one store per city uses:
e: Exclusive distribution protects brand image and dealer margins.

q: Offering a consistent experience across website, app and physical stores is:
e: Omnichannel integrates channels into one seamless customer experience.

q: Disagreement between a manufacturer and its retailers over pricing is:
e: Channel conflict arises when members' goals clash.

q: The specific group of customers a business aims to reach is its:
e: A target market is the segment a firm chooses to serve.

q: Dividing customers by age, income and gender is ____ segmentation.
e: Demographic variables describe measurable population traits.

q: Segmenting by lifestyles, values and interests is ____ segmentation.
e: Psychographics capture attitudes and lifestyles.

q: The image of a product in customers' minds relative to competitors is its:
e: Positioning defines how a brand is perceived versus rivals.

q: A marketing plan's objectives should be:
e: Measurable objectives let marketers evaluate results.

q: Segmenting by how often customers buy or how loyal they are is ____ segmentation.
e: Behavioral segmentation uses usage rate, loyalty and benefits sought.

q: Data a company collects itself for a specific purpose, such as a survey, is:
e: Primary data is gathered firsthand; secondary data already exists.

q: A small group discussion led by a moderator to explore opinions is a:
e: Focus groups give qualitative insight into attitudes.

q: The first step in the marketing research process is to:
e: A clear problem definition guides the entire study.

q: A question that leads respondents toward a certain answer creates:
e: Leading questions bias results and reduce accuracy.

q: Testing two versions of an email to see which gets more clicks is:
e: A/B tests compare variations with real users.

q: Numerical data that can be measured and analyzed statistically is:
e: Quantitative data is numeric; qualitative captures opinions and descriptions.

q: Predicting future sales based on past data and trends is:
e: Forecasts drive inventory, staffing and budgets.

q: A sample in which every member of the population has an equal chance of selection is:
e: Random sampling reduces selection bias.

q: Setting a high initial price for a new innovative product, then lowering it, is:
e: Skimming captures early adopters willing to pay more.

q: Pricing an item at $9.99 instead of $10.00 is:
e: Odd-even (psychological) pricing makes prices seem lower.

q: A product costs $40 and is marked up 25% on cost. The selling price is:
Entering a market with a low price to gain market share quickly is:
e: Penetration pricing builds volume and share fast.

q: Selling an item below cost to attract shoppers who buy other products is using a:
e: Loss leaders drive traffic that leads to profitable purchases.

q: Changing prices in real time based on demand, like ride-share surge pricing, is:
e: Dynamic pricing adjusts to supply and demand conditions.

q: Offering a meal combo for less than buying items separately is:
e: Bundling increases perceived value and average sale.

q: The stage of the product life cycle where sales grow fastest is:
e: In growth, sales and competition rise rapidly.

q: All the products a company sells make up its:
e: Product mix = all product lines offered.

q: Services differ from goods because they are intangible, perishable, inseparable and:
e: Service quality varies by provider and occasion.

q: A brand name used by a retailer for products made by others (e.g., a store brand) is a:
e: Private labels typically carry higher retailer margins.

q: Using an established brand name on a new product category is:
e: Extensions leverage existing brand equity.

q: Packaging serves to protect, promote and:
e: Packages inform buyers through labels, ingredients and instructions.

q: The value of a brand beyond the product itself, built through customer perceptions, is:
e: Brand equity allows premium pricing and loyalty.

q: In the maturity stage, a common strategy is to:
c: Find new uses or markets to extend the life cycle
e: Firms extend maturity through modification, new markets or new uses.

q: The promotional mix includes advertising, personal selling, sales promotion and:
e: The promotional mix also includes PR (and often digital/direct marketing).

q: Free media coverage of a company's event is:
e: Publicity is unpaid media attention, often earned through PR.

q: Coupons, samples and contests are forms of:
e: Sales promotions are short-term incentives to buy now.

q: Paying a social media creator to feature a product is:
e: Influencer marketing leverages creators' trust with their audience.

q: AIDA stands for attention, interest, desire and:
e: AIDA models how promotions move buyers toward purchase.

q: The number of different people exposed to an ad at least once is its:
e: Reach = unique audience; frequency = average times each sees it.

q: Coordinating all promotional messages so they send one consistent brand message is:
e: IMC aligns every touchpoint around one message.

q: A manufacturer and retailer sharing the cost of a local ad is:
e: Co-op advertising splits cost and benefits both parties.

q: An ad promoting a company's image rather than a specific product is:
e: Institutional ads build goodwill and reputation.

q: The first step of the selling process is usually:
e: The common steps: approach, determine needs, present, handle objections, close, suggestion sell, follow up (with prospecting/pre-approach before for B2B).

q: Explaining how a product's feature helps the customer is turning a feature into a:
e: Customers buy benefits — what the feature does for them.

q: A customer says, 'This is more than I wanted to spend.' This is a(n):
e: Objections signal concerns; address them by focusing on value.

q: Recommending a phone case to someone buying a phone is:
e: Suggesting related items increases sale value and satisfaction.

q: Searching for potential customers is called:
e: Prospecting finds and qualifies leads.

q: Asking 'Would you like it in black or silver?' is a(n):
e: The alternative close lets the customer choose between two yes options.

q: Contacting a customer after the sale to ensure satisfaction is:
e: Follow-up builds relationships and repeat sales.

q: Encouraging a customer to buy a higher-end version of a product is:
e: Upselling moves the customer to a premium option.

q: Gross pay minus taxes and other deductions equals:
e: Net (take-home) pay is what remains after deductions.

q: Which form tells your employer how much federal income tax to withhold?
e: The W-4 sets withholding; the W-2 reports annual wages.

q: FICA taxes fund:
e: FICA withholds Social Security and Medicare taxes.

q: Generally, more education and training lead to:
e: Human capital investment typically raises earning potential.

q: Income from investments like interest and dividends is:
e: Unearned income comes from assets rather than work.

q: A freelancer receives which tax form from clients instead of a W-2?
e: Independent contractors receive 1099 forms and pay self-employment tax.

q: A spending plan that matches income to expenses is a:
e: Budgets help control spending and reach goals.

q: Rent and car payments that stay the same each month are:
e: Fixed expenses are predictable; variable ones change monthly.

q: Comparing the price per ounce of two cereal boxes uses:
e: Unit price lets you compare value across package sizes.

q: The 50/30/20 rule suggests spending 50% of after-tax income on:
e: 50% needs, 30% wants, 20% savings and debt repayment.

q: Buying something unplanned because of an emotional urge is:
e: Impulse buys can derail budgets; waiting periods help.

q: Savings set aside for unexpected costs like car repairs is an:
e: Experts often recommend 3–6 months of expenses.

q: Earning interest on both your deposit and previously earned interest is:
e: Compounding makes savings grow faster over time.

q: The FDIC insures bank deposits up to:
c: $250,000 per depositor, per bank, per ownership category
e: FDIC insurance covers up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, per ownership category.

q: 'Pay yourself first' means:
c: Saving before spending on other things
e: Automating savings first builds the habit.

q: The Rule of 72 estimates:
c: How long it takes money to double
e: Years to double ≈ 72 ÷ annual interest rate.

q: Spreading money across many investments to reduce risk is:
e: Diversification limits the impact of any one investment's loss.

q: Buying a share of stock makes you a(n):
e: Stockholders own equity; bondholders are lenders.

q: Generally, investments with higher potential returns carry:
e: The risk-return tradeoff.

q: A fund that tracks a market index like the S&P 500 at low cost is a(n):
e: Index funds offer broad diversification with low fees.

q: A retirement account where contributions are taxed now but withdrawals in retirement are tax-free is a:
e: Roth accounts use after-tax money; qualified withdrawals are tax-free.

q: Matching contributions an employer adds to your 401(k) are best described as:
e: Contribute at least enough to get the full match.

q: The most important factor in a FICO credit score is:
e: Payment history is about 35% of a FICO score.

q: APR stands for:
e: APR is the yearly cost of borrowing, including some fees.

q: Paying only the minimum on a credit card balance usually results in:
c: Paying much more interest over time
e: Interest keeps accruing on the remaining balance.

q: Credit utilization is the ratio of:
e: Keeping utilization low (often under 30%) helps your score.

q: You can get free copies of your credit reports from:
e: AnnualCreditReport.com is the official free source.

q: A loan backed by an asset the lender can take if you don't pay is:
e: Auto loans and mortgages are secured by the car or home.

q: The amount you pay out of pocket before insurance begins to pay is the:
e: Higher deductibles usually mean lower premiums.

q: The regular payment made to keep an insurance policy active is the:
e: Premiums are paid monthly, semiannually or annually.

q: Using someone else's personal information to open accounts is:
e: Monitoring reports and freezing credit help prevent identity theft.

q: Which insurance covers damage you cause to others in a car accident?
e: Liability pays for others' injuries and property damage; it is required in most states.

q: Renters insurance mainly protects:
e: The landlord insures the building; renters insure their possessions.

q: Locking your credit so new accounts can't be opened is a:
e: Freezes are free and block new credit in your name.

q: A manager needs to deliver detailed, complex instructions that employees will refer back to later. The best channel is:
e: Written messages create a permanent record people can review, which suits detailed or complex information.

q: Which is an example of a barrier caused by semantics?
c: Using a word the listener interprets differently
e: Semantic barriers come from differences in the meaning of words or jargon.

q: When delivering bad news to a customer in writing, it is usually best to:
c: State the bad news in the subject line in capitals
Open with a neutral buffer, explain the reasons, then give the news and an alternative
e: The indirect approach softens bad news and preserves goodwill by explaining reasons before the decision.

q: An employee nods, maintains eye contact and asks clarifying questions while a coworker explains a problem. This employee is:
e: Nonverbal attention and clarifying questions are signs of active listening.

q: The person who encodes and sends a message in the communication process is the:
e: The sender encodes the idea into a message and chooses a channel to transmit it.

q: Which is the most professional way to handle a phone call you must put on hold?
c: Put the caller on hold without speaking
Ask permission and wait for the caller's reply before placing them on hold
Tell the caller to call back
Cover the receiver and talk to a coworker
e: Asking permission and waiting for a response respects the caller's time and preferences.

q: A brief, informal summary of the most important points at the start of a long business report is the:
e: An executive summary lets busy readers grasp the key findings and recommendations quickly.

q: A loyalty program that gives a free coffee after every ten purchases is mainly designed to:
e: Reward programs give customers a reason to come back, building repeat business.

q: Employees are allowed to resolve complaints up to $50 without asking a manager. This practice is called:
e: Empowering front-line employees speeds up service recovery and increases customer satisfaction.

q: A business sends a short survey after every purchase. Its main purpose is to:
c: Gather customer feedback to improve service
e: Feedback shows where the customer experience succeeds or fails so the business can improve.

q: A difficult customer becomes rude while complaining. The employee should:
c: Stay calm, avoid taking it personally, and focus on solving the problem
Argue the facts until the customer agrees
e: Remaining calm and solution-focused de-escalates the situation and protects the relationship.

q: When two goods are substitutes, an increase in the price of one will usually:
c: Have no effect on the other
e: If coffee gets more expensive, some buyers switch to tea, so demand for the substitute rises.

q: The price at which quantity supplied equals quantity demanded is the:
e: At equilibrium the market clears with no surplus or shortage.

q: A government-set maximum price, such as rent control, is a:
e: A price ceiling caps prices below equilibrium and often creates shortages.

q: In a market economy, the basic questions of what, how and for whom to produce are answered mainly by:
e: Market economies rely on prices and private decisions to allocate resources.

q: A team member is visibly upset after a meeting. A leader with strong emotional intelligence would most likely:
e: Recognizing others' emotions and responding with support builds trust.

q: Which is an example of intrinsic motivation?
c: Working hard because you enjoy the challenge
e: Intrinsic motivation comes from internal satisfaction rather than external rewards.

q: Stress at work is best managed by:
c: Prioritizing tasks, taking short breaks and asking for help when needed
e: Planning, rest and support are healthy, effective stress-management strategies.

q: An employee discovers a coworker padding their expense report. The most ethical action is to:
c: Report it through the proper channel
e: Ethical behavior includes reporting misconduct through appropriate, confidential channels.

q: When a team follows one strong voice without questioning a flawed plan to avoid conflict, it is called:
e: Groupthink suppresses dissent and leads to poor decisions.

q: Treating every customer and coworker with respect regardless of background demonstrates:
e: Valuing people of all backgrounds is part of professional, inclusive behavior.

q: A manager says, 'I can see you put a lot of effort into this report.' This is an example of:
e: Recognizing effort boosts morale and motivation.

q: Influencing others to accept an idea by showing how it benefits them is:
e: Ethical persuasion appeals to others' interests and gives sound reasons.

q: In a negotiation, a win-win outcome means:
c: Both sides leave with their key interests met
e: Collaborative negotiation seeks outcomes that satisfy both parties' core interests.

q: Accepting responsibility for a mistake and explaining how you will fix it shows:
e: Accountability builds credibility and trust with supervisors and coworkers.

q: A positive attitude at work is most likely to result in:
e: Positive attitudes spread to coworkers and customers and improve performance.

q: A business owner who uses personal savings and early sales revenue instead of investors is:
e: Bootstrapping keeps full ownership but limits growth to available cash.

q: Raising small amounts of money from many people through an online platform is:
e: Crowdfunding sites let many backers each contribute small amounts.

q: Which part of a business plan describes the target market, competitors and industry trends?
e: The market analysis shows the entrepreneur understands customers and competition.

q: An entrepreneur who starts a new venture inside an existing company is called a(n):
e: Intrapreneurs innovate within established organizations.

q: A potential customer's strongest reason to buy from a new business instead of a competitor is its:
e: A USP clearly states what makes the business different and better for its target customer.

q: Before launching, an entrepreneur interviews 30 potential customers about their problems. This is an example of:
e: Customer discovery tests whether a real problem and demand exist before investing heavily.

q: Selling a business or taking it public so founders can cash out is part of the:
e: Investors want to know how and when they might realize a return through an exit.

q: A company's net income is $30,000 on revenue of $200,000. Its net profit margin is:
e: Net profit margin = net income ÷ revenue = 30,000 ÷ 200,000 = 15%.

q: Total liabilities are $80,000 and owner's equity is $120,000. Total assets are:
e: Assets = liabilities + equity = 80,000 + 120,000 = $200,000.

q: Which is an operating expense?
e: Utilities are ongoing operating expenses; buying a van is a capital expenditure.

q: A product sells for $40 with a variable cost of $25. Its contribution margin per unit is:
e: Contribution margin = price − variable cost = 40 − 25 = $15.

q: A business wants to know if it can pay bills due in the next few months. It should look mainly at:
e: Liquidity measures the ability to meet short-term obligations.

q: The debt-to-equity ratio measures:
c: How much a company relies on borrowing compared with owner investment
e: A high debt-to-equity ratio signals more financial leverage and risk.

q: A budget variance occurs when:
c: Actual results differ from budgeted amounts
e: Variance analysis compares actual to planned figures to find problems or opportunities.

q: Revenue is $500,000, cost of goods sold is $300,000 and operating expenses are $150,000. Operating income is:
e: Gross profit 200,000 − operating expenses 150,000 = $50,000 operating income.

q: A $1,000 investment earns $80 in one year. The annual rate of return is:
Which statement shows how cash moved through operating, investing and financing activities?
e: The statement of cash flows explains changes in the cash balance.

q: Borrowing money to buy a building would appear in which section of the cash flow statement?
e: The loan proceeds are a financing inflow; buying the building is an investing outflow.

q: Profits a company keeps instead of paying out as dividends are:
e: Retained earnings accumulate in equity and can fund growth.

q: Fixed costs are $24,000. Each unit sells for $30 and costs $18 to make. How many units must be sold to earn a $12,000 profit?
e: (Fixed costs + target profit) ÷ contribution margin = 36,000 ÷ 12 = 3,000 units.

q: A sales forecast predicts $90,000 in sales; actual sales are $81,000. Sales fell short of forecast by:
e: Shortfall = 9,000 ÷ 90,000 = 10% below forecast.

q: Which action would most directly improve a business's cash flow?
c: Paying suppliers early without a discount
e: Collecting receivables sooner brings cash in faster.

q: Comparing a company's financial ratios over five years is called:
e: Trend analysis shows whether performance is improving or declining over time.

q: Expenses that have been paid in advance, like six months of insurance, are recorded as:
e: Prepaid expenses are assets until the benefit is used up.

q: Inventory turnover is calculated as:
c: Cost of goods sold ÷ average inventory
e: It shows how many times inventory is sold and replaced during the period.

q: A business borrows $10,000 at 6% simple annual interest for 2 years. Total interest owed is:
e: Simple interest = principal × rate × time = 10,000 × 0.06 × 2 = $1,200.

q: A company uses data about past purchases to predict which customers will buy again. This is:
e: Predictive analytics uses historical data to forecast future behavior.

q: Converting data into a code so only authorized users can read it is:
e: Encryption protects data in storage and transmission.

q: Software that blocks unauthorized access to a network is a:
e: Firewalls filter incoming and outgoing traffic based on security rules.

q: Customer relationship management (CRM) software primarily stores:
e: CRM systems centralize customer data so teams can personalize service and sales.

q: Which is the best example of a strong password practice?
c: Using a long, unique passphrase for each account
Writing it on a sticky note on your monitor
e: Long, unique passphrases resist guessing and limit damage if one account is breached.

q: Malicious software that locks files until a payment is made is:
e: Ransomware encrypts data and demands payment; backups are the best defense.

q: Checking several reliable sources before using information in a report is called:
e: Verification ensures the information is accurate and credible.

q: The extra inventory kept on hand to avoid running out during unexpected demand is:
e: Safety stock buffers against demand spikes and supplier delays.

q: Receiving goods and checking them against the purchase order and invoice is part of:
e: Checking shipments catches shortages, damage and billing errors.

q: A restaurant schedules more servers on Friday nights than Tuesday afternoons. This is an example of:
e: Scheduling to forecasted demand controls labor costs while maintaining service.

q: Preventive maintenance on equipment is done mainly to:
e: Regular maintenance prevents failures that interrupt operations.

q: Which is the best reason to get bids from several suppliers?
c: To compare price, quality and reliability
e: Competitive bids help a business choose the best overall value.

q: A government agency that sets and enforces workplace safety standards in the U.S. is:
e: The Occupational Safety and Health Administration regulates workplace safety.

q: Lean operations focus on:
e: Lean methods remove steps that don't add value for the customer.

q: A store's security policy requires two employees when opening the safe. This primarily helps prevent:
e: Dual control reduces the opportunity for employee theft.

q: Tracking each product with barcodes or RFID tags mainly improves:
e: Automatic identification keeps inventory records accurate and current.

q: The document a buyer sends to a supplier to order goods is a:
e: The purchase order states what is being bought, the quantity and the price.

q: The bill a supplier sends requesting payment for goods delivered is an:
e: An invoice lists what was shipped and the amount due.

q: Reordering inventory automatically when stock falls to a set level uses a:
e: A reorder point triggers replenishment before stock runs out.

q: Which is an example of an emergency procedure every employee should know?
e: Knowing evacuation procedures protects employees and customers during emergencies.

q: Using fewer suppliers but building closer long-term relationships with them can lead to:
e: Strategic supplier partnerships often improve quality, pricing and responsiveness.

q: A business's productivity rises when it:
c: Produces more output with the same or fewer inputs
Hires more staff for the same output
e: Productivity is output per unit of input.

q: Disposing of hazardous materials according to regulations is part of a business's:
e: Proper disposal protects people and the environment and avoids fines.

q: A document that summarizes your education, experience and skills for employers is a:
e: A résumé is a concise overview of qualifications for a job.

q: Which is the best answer to 'What is your greatest weakness?' in an interview?
c: A real weakness plus the steps you are taking to improve it
A strength disguised as a weakness with no detail
e: Honest self-awareness plus a plan to improve shows maturity.

q: An informational interview is a meeting to:
c: Learn about a career from someone working in it
e: Informational interviews build knowledge and networks without asking for a job directly.

q: A collection of your best work samples, such as projects and designs, is a:
e: Portfolios give employers concrete evidence of skills.

q: Arriving early, dressing appropriately and being prepared for work demonstrates:
e: Professional behaviors build a reputation for reliability.

q: Accepting criticism from a supervisor and using it to improve shows you are:
e: Being coachable accelerates growth and earns trust.

q: A person you list who can confirm your work habits to an employer is a:
e: References vouch for your character and performance; always ask permission first.

q: A company decides to compete by offering the lowest prices in its industry. This strategy is:
e: Cost leaders win by operating more efficiently than rivals.

q: Analyzing political, economic, social and technological factors in the environment is a:
e: PEST analysis scans the external environment for opportunities and threats.

q: Measuring actual performance against goals and taking corrective action is the management function of:
e: Controlling closes the loop between plans and results.

q: Storing customer service answers in a searchable database so all reps give consistent answers is an example of:
e: Knowledge bases capture answers once and make them reusable.

q: When an experienced employee retires without documenting key processes, the company risks:
e: Undocumented expertise leaves with the person; KM practices help prevent this.

q: A document that formally authorizes a project and defines its objectives and sponsor is the:
e: The charter gives the project manager authority and sets the project's purpose.

q: Workers' compensation insurance covers:
e: Workers' comp pays medical costs and lost wages for job-related injuries.

q: A business that sells products that might injure customers should carry:
e: Product liability insurance covers claims that a product caused harm.

q: Identifying risks, rating their likelihood and impact, and deciding how to handle them is:
e: Risk assessment prioritizes which risks deserve the most attention.

q: A manufacturer that sells to wholesalers, who sell to retailers, who sell to consumers, uses a:
e: Each added intermediary lengthens the channel.

q: Watching how shoppers move through a store without asking them questions is:
e: Observation records actual behavior rather than reported behavior.

q: Government census reports used by a marketer are an example of:
e: Secondary data was collected by someone else for another purpose.

q: A survey gives consistent results when repeated under the same conditions. The survey is:
e: Reliability means consistency; validity means measuring what you intended.

q: Website analytics show 2,000 visitors and 60 purchases. The conversion rate is:
e: Conversion rate = 60 ÷ 2,000 = 3%.

q: Which question is most appropriate for a customer satisfaction survey?
c: 'Don't you agree our service is excellent?'
'How satisfied were you with your visit, from 1 to 5?'
e: A neutral rating scale avoids leading the respondent and collects comparable data.

q: A marketing information system (MkIS) is used to:
c: Gather, organize and analyze data for marketing decisions
e: An MkIS turns ongoing data into information managers can act on.

q: Testing a new product in a few cities before a national launch is:
e: Test markets reveal demand and problems at lower risk.

q: The group of people a researcher wants to learn about is the:
e: The sample is the subset actually studied to draw conclusions about the population.

q: Adding a new flavor to an existing snack line is an example of:
e: Line extensions add variations within an existing product line.

q: A written promise that a product will perform as stated or be repaired or replaced is a:
e: Warranties reduce buyer risk and build confidence.

q: The stage of the product life cycle with low sales, high costs and few competitors is:
e: New products need heavy promotion while awareness is low.

q: Products bought frequently with little effort, like gum and milk, are:
e: Convenience goods are low-cost, routine purchases.

q: Customers compare several brands on price and quality before buying a laptop. A laptop is a:
e: Shopping goods involve comparison of features and prices.

q: A hotel's service quality varies depending on which employee helps a guest. This reflects services being:
e: Training and standards help reduce service variability.

q: Dropping a product that no longer earns a profit is called:
e: Removing weak products frees resources for stronger ones.

q: An ad that directly compares a brand with a named competitor is:
e: Comparative ads highlight advantages over specific rivals.

q: Paying to have a product appear in a TV show or movie is:
e: Product placement integrates brands into entertainment content.

q: Social media posts, websites and search ads are examples of:
e: Digital channels allow targeting and measurable results.

q: The total amount of money a business plans to spend on promotion in a period is its:
e: Budgets can be set by percentage of sales, objective-and-task or competitive parity.

q: Repeating a customer's concern before answering it, such as 'So you're worried about battery life,' helps the salesperson:
c: Show understanding and clarify the objection
e: Restating confirms understanding and shows the customer they were heard.

q: A list of all accounts and their balances used to check that debits equal credits is a:
e: The trial balance checks the mathematical accuracy of the ledger.

q: Money a business owes to suppliers is recorded as:
e: Accounts payable is a current liability.

q: Publicly traded companies must file financial reports with the:
e: The SEC requires public companies to disclose financial information to investors.

q: A record of transactions in the order they occur is a:
e: Transactions are first recorded in the journal, then posted to ledger accounts.

q: Financial software that automatically categorizes transactions mainly helps a business:
c: Save time and reduce recording errors
e: Automation improves accuracy and frees time for analysis.

q: The principle that expenses should be recorded in the same period as the revenue they helped earn is the:
e: Matching gives an accurate picture of profit for each period.

q: Maya earns $15 per hour and works 30 hours a week. Her weekly gross pay is:
e: Gross pay = hourly rate × hours = 15 × 30 = $450.

q: Under federal law, most hourly employees must be paid overtime at what rate for hours over 40 in a workweek?
e: The Fair Labor Standards Act requires time-and-a-half for covered nonexempt workers.

q: Jordan earns $20 an hour and works 44 hours in one week. With time-and-a-half overtime, gross pay is:
The form an employer sends each January showing your total wages and taxes withheld for the year is the:
e: Employees use the W-2 to file their income tax return.

q: A fixed annual amount of pay that does not depend on hours worked is a:
e: Salaried employees receive the same pay each period regardless of exact hours.

q: Which is NOT usually a payroll deduction?
e: Sales tax is paid on purchases, not withheld from paychecks.

q: The U.S. federal income tax is called progressive because:
c: Higher portions of income are taxed at higher rates
e: Income is taxed in brackets, with higher rates on higher portions of income.

q: If too much tax was withheld from your paychecks during the year, after filing you will:
e: A refund returns the amount withheld beyond what you actually owe.

q: The annual deadline to file a federal income tax return is usually:
e: Returns are typically due April 15, unless it falls on a weekend or holiday or an extension is filed.

q: Employer-provided health insurance, paid vacation and retirement matching are examples of:
e: Benefits add value to total compensation beyond wages.

q: Self-employed people pay self-employment tax to cover:
e: They pay both the employee and employer shares of these payroll taxes.

q: Two job offers pay the same salary, but one includes health insurance. The job with insurance has:
e: Compare total compensation, not just salary, when evaluating offers.

q: Which factor most often increases a worker's earning potential?
e: Skills that employers value command higher pay.

q: An employee's gross pay is $600 and deductions total $132. Net pay is:
The form new employees complete to prove they are eligible to work in the U.S. is the:
e: Employers must verify identity and work authorization with Form I-9.

q: Earning money from a side business such as selling crafts online is income that:
c: Generally must be reported for taxes
e: Self-employment and side-gig income is generally taxable and must be reported.

q: Interest earned in a savings account is:
e: Interest is generally taxable and is reported on a 1099-INT.

q: Entrepreneurship as a way to earn income involves:
c: Higher risk with potential for higher reward
e: Business owners earn profits but bear the risk of losses.

q: A tax credit reduces:
e: A credit cuts tax owed directly; a deduction lowers taxable income.

q: A smart first step before making a large purchase is to:
c: Compare prices, features and reviews from several sellers
Use the first ad you see
e: Comparison shopping helps you get the best value.

q: Buying a used car instead of a new one mainly helps a buyer avoid:
e: New cars lose a large share of their value in the first few years.

q: An item is $80 with a 25% discount. The sale price is:
Money left after paying for necessities that can be spent on wants is:
e: Discretionary income is spent on non-essentials or saved.

q: Tracking every expense for a month is useful because it:
e: Tracking reveals spending patterns to adjust in a budget.

q: A 'buy now, pay later' plan can hurt a budget mainly because:
c: It makes it easy to overspend and miss payments
e: Splitting payments can hide total cost and lead to fees if payments are missed.

q: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) mainly:
c: Protects consumers in financial products and services
e: The CFPB enforces consumer financial protection laws and takes complaints.

q: Monthly subscriptions you forget to cancel are an example of:
c: Spending leaks that hurt a budget
e: Small recurring charges add up; review them regularly.

q: Leasing a car differs from buying it because with a lease you:
c: Pay to use the car for a set time without owning it
e: Leases often include mileage limits and wear charges, and you don't build ownership.

q: An account that typically pays a higher interest rate than a regular savings account while keeping money accessible is a:
e: High-yield savings accounts, often online, pay more while staying liquid.

q: You deposit $1,000 at 5% interest compounded annually. After 2 years you have about:
Using the Rule of 72, money earning 6% per year doubles in about:
Inflation affects savings by:
c: Reducing the purchasing power of money over time
e: If savings earn less than inflation, they buy less in the future.

q: Setting up an automatic transfer to savings each payday helps because it:
c: Makes saving consistent without relying on willpower
e: Automation turns saving into a habit.

q: A certificate of deposit (CD) usually pays more than a savings account because you:
c: Agree to leave the money deposited for a set term
Can withdraw anytime with no penalty
e: Early withdrawal from a CD usually costs a penalty.

q: APY (annual percentage yield) on a savings account shows:
e: APY lets you compare savings accounts with different compounding schedules.

q: Saving money for a specific purchase in six months is a:
e: Short-term goals usually span a year or less.

q: A 529 plan is a tax-advantaged account designed to save for:
e: 529 plans offer tax benefits when funds are used for qualified education costs.

q: Starting to save at age 20 instead of 30 usually results in much more money at retirement mainly because of:
e: Extra years of compounding have a large effect on final balances.

q: A bond pays its owner:
c: Interest, with the principal repaid at maturity
e: Bonds are loans to the issuer that pay interest.

q: A mutual fund pools money from many investors to:
c: Buy a diversified portfolio managed by professionals
e: Funds provide diversification and professional management.

q: An exchange-traded fund (ETF) differs from a traditional mutual fund mainly because it:
c: Trades on an exchange throughout the day like a stock
e: ETFs trade at market prices during the trading day.

q: A portion of company profits paid to shareholders is a:
e: Not all companies pay dividends; many reinvest profits instead.

q: Which investment generally has the highest risk and highest potential return over the long term?
e: Stocks are volatile short-term but have historically returned more over long periods.

q: Investing the same amount at regular intervals regardless of price is:
e: It reduces the risk of investing a lump sum at a bad time.

q: An expense ratio of 1% on a $10,000 fund investment costs about how much per year?
e: 1% of 10,000 = $100 each year.

q: Profit from selling an investment for more than you paid is a:
e: Capital gains may be taxed when the investment is sold.

q: A person's risk tolerance describes:
c: How much investment loss they can accept for potential gain
e: Risk tolerance depends on goals, time horizon and comfort with volatility.

q: A 401(k) is a:
e: Employees contribute through payroll, often with an employer match.

q: Contributions to a traditional IRA or traditional 401(k) are generally:
c: Made before taxes, with withdrawals taxed in retirement
e: Traditional accounts defer taxes until withdrawal; Roth accounts are the reverse.

q: A promise of 'guaranteed high returns with no risk' is a warning sign of:
e: Legitimate investments always carry some risk; guarantees of high returns are a red flag.

q: A long time horizon generally allows an investor to:
c: Take more risk because there is time to recover from downturns
e: Younger investors can usually ride out market volatility.

q: Buying a home can be considered an investment because:
c: It may appreciate in value and builds equity
e: Homes can build wealth but also carry costs and risks, and they are not liquid.

q: Spreading investments across stocks, bonds and cash based on goals is called:
e: Asset allocation balances risk and return across asset classes.

q: A credit score typically ranges from:
e: Common FICO and VantageScore models range from 300 to 850.

q: A credit card has a $2,000 limit and a $500 balance. Credit utilization is:
e: Utilization = 500 ÷ 2,000 = 25%.

q: Which action will most likely lower a credit score?
e: Late payments are the most damaging factor for credit scores.

q: A loan with an interest rate that can change over time is a:
e: Variable rates can rise, increasing payments.

q: A cosigner on a loan:
c: Is legally responsible for the debt if the borrower doesn't pay
e: Cosigning is a serious legal obligation.

q: Short-term, high-cost loans due on your next payday are:
e: Payday loans often carry extremely high APRs and can trap borrowers in debt.

q: The Fair Credit Reporting Act gives consumers the right to:
c: Dispute inaccurate information on their credit reports
e: Credit bureaus must investigate disputes about inaccurate information.

q: A debit card differs from a credit card because a debit card:
c: Draws money directly from your bank account
e: Debit cards spend your own money; credit cards are loans.

q: Paying the full credit card statement balance by the due date means you:
c: Usually pay no interest on purchases
e: Most cards offer a grace period on purchases when the balance is paid in full.

q: The amount of money originally borrowed on a loan is the:
e: Interest is charged on the outstanding principal.

q: Federal student loans differ from most private student loans because they often offer:
e: Federal loans have protections like income-driven repayment and deferment options.

q: A longer loan term with the same interest rate usually means:
c: Lower monthly payments but more total interest
Higher monthly payments and less interest
e: Stretching payments lowers each payment but increases total cost.

q: Applying for many new credit cards in a short time can lower a score because of:
c: Multiple hard inquiries and new accounts
e: Hard inquiries and many new accounts can signal risk to lenders.

q: The debt-to-income ratio lenders use compares:
c: Monthly debt payments to gross monthly income
e: A lower DTI makes borrowers more likely to be approved.

q: Which is the best first step if you can't make a loan payment on time?
c: Contact the lender to discuss options before the due date
Open a new card to pay it
e: Lenders may offer hardship plans if contacted early.

q: Health insurance where you pay a fixed amount, such as $25, for a doctor visit uses a:
e: Copays are set fees for covered services.

q: Life insurance is most important for someone who:
c: Has dependents who rely on their income
e: Life insurance replaces income for dependents after the policyholder's death.

q: Term life insurance differs from whole life insurance because term life:
c: Covers a set period and is usually cheaper
Lasts forever and builds cash value
e: Term policies are pure protection for a fixed period.

q: Disability insurance protects against:
c: Loss of income if you can't work due to illness or injury
e: It replaces part of your income during a qualifying disability.

q: Choosing a higher insurance deductible usually:
e: You take on more of small losses in exchange for lower premiums.

q: Collision coverage on an auto policy pays for:
c: Damage to your own car from an accident
Theft of items in your home
e: Collision covers your vehicle; liability covers others.

q: Comprehensive auto coverage pays for damage from:
c: Theft, hail, fire or hitting an animal
e: Comprehensive covers non-collision events.

q: Shredding old bank statements before throwing them away helps prevent:
e: Documents with personal information can be used by identity thieves.

q: The person named to receive a life insurance payout is the:
e: Beneficiaries receive the death benefit.
